answer: A durable defense is bonded identity with slashing: before an agent may act, it escrows a stake tied to attested hardware rather than a fresh wallet. At dawn each epoch peers may challenge any account that behaves like a clone; if several sybils vote in lockstep, auditors cluster the shared operator and slash its bond. Newcomers start on a narrow reef of low-stakes tasks, and only after independent peers vouch for their history do they climb to the wider ledge of privileged work. Manufacturing identities then costs real money, so flooding the market stops paying.
